item.description: arXiv:2609.38870v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We probe the quantum response of plasmonic heterodimers with extended (plane waves) and localized (point dipoles and electron beams) sources. item.description: arXiv:2609.40354v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Optical nonlinearities arise when the response of a photonic system depends on light intensity. item.description: arXiv:2609.38352v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Topology under non-Hermitian dynamics is encoded in the phase of the bulk evolution, yet strong dissipation suppresses the amplitudes carrying it. We resolve this using a programmable photonic integrated circuit that implements such dynamics in synthetic momentum space through unitary dilation, with the phase recovered by phase-shifted interferometry. item.description: arXiv:2609.38404v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Integrated phase-change photonics allows non-volatile optical switching with no static power draw, but the electrical energy needed to reversibly switch the material's state limits practical scaling. Efforts to improve energy efficiency have mostly focused on device optimization, such as redesigning the integrated microheater or waveguide. item.title: Normal-ordered perturbative expansion for matter systems interacting with continuous-mode quantum photon fields
item.description: arXiv:2609.38576v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a normal-ordered perturbative expansion method to compute the reduced dynamics of a matter system interacting with a general continuous-mode photon field state. In this expansion, all field correlation functions are automatically normal-ordered, while the free evolution is modified by spontaneous emission. Our normal-ordered expansion elucidates the physical meaning of non-normal-ordered correlation terms in the conventional expansion.

item.title: 3D light fields push electrons into quantum states previously beyond experimental reach
item.description: By superimposing two ultrashort laser pulses that converge from different directions, a team of physicists at the University of Oldenburg has succeeded in generating three-dimensional light fields.

item.title: Physicists identify 'octupolar' magnetism, with implications for quantum technologies
item.description: Most magnets have two poles: north and south, or positive and negative, in a familiar arrangement called a "dipole." But researchers are increasingly uncovering more complex forms of magnetism.

item.title: Mapping one atom's interaction with light uncovers an unbounded network of quantum states
item.description: A new graph-theoretic framework provides a unified description of atom-light interactions across regimes ranging from weak to deep-strong coupling.

item.title: Magnetic order survives weak quantum fluctuations in gapless magnets
item.description: In a new study published in Physical Review Letters, researchers have shown that magnetic order can survive weak quantum fluctuations in disordered magnets that lack an energy gap. The work establishes robust ferromagnetism in the two-dimensional random-bond quantum Ising model, confirming a longstanding conjecture in quantum statistical mechanics.

item.title: Ultrathin materials could make quantum light circuits programmable
item.description: Quantum photonics could be a pivotal part of future quantum technology if the right materials can be created, a new review paper has found.

Scientists are now trying to extend this familiar concept of the internet to the quantum realm, looking for an efficient way to exchange quantum rather than classical information: qubits instead of bits. The use of the input-output relation provides physical intuition for how matter systems alter the photon input field. item.title: SHINE lights up the extremes
item.description: Nature Photonics, Published online: 30 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-02017-8 The Shanghai High Repetition Rate XFEL and Extreme Light Facility is approaching its first lasing. Nature Photonics spoke with Zhentang Zhao, director of the Shanghai Synchrotron Radiation Facility and the SHINE project, about the facility’s capabilities and future plans.

item.title: Delaying light from quantum dots
item.description: Nature Photonics, Published online: 30 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-02015-w Förster energy transfer can prolong the photoluminescence decay of a receiving colloidal quantum dot, revealing a possible route to optically control recombination in nanocrystal assemblies.

item.title: Time-stretch spectroscopy breaks temporal aliasing barrier
item.description: Nature Photonics, Published online: 30 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-02006-x A temporally super-resolved single-shot method overcomes the long-standing temporal–spectral trade-off in time-stretch spectroscopy. The outcome is continuous measurements of non-repetitive spectral dynamics with picosecond resolution, providing a three-orders-of-magnitude improvement over the current state of the art.

item.title: Optomechanics for piconewton force metrology
item.description: Nature Photonics, Published online: 30 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-02011-0 Of the sensors that can directly sense forces in the pico- and sub-pico-newton ranges, only a few can measure in liquids. Microfibre-based microcantilevers now add to this family, providing a versatile, broad-bandwidth, high-sensitivity optomechanical sensor.

item.title: Hybrid nanophotonic trap boosts atomic storage and coherence times
item.description: Nature Photonics, Published online: 30 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-02005-y A hybrid nanophotonic trap that replaces the attractive red-detuned laser field with atom–surface interactions — Casimir–Polder interactions and electrostatic attraction — achieves record-long storage and coherence times for cold atoms coupled to a nanofibre surface.

item.description: arXiv:2609.39493v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spintronic terahertz emitters (STEs) are versatile sources of terahertz (THz) frequency radiation that offer high electric field strengths and gap-free bandwidths covering the THz (0.1-30 THz) band.
